speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In that speech, I said, "Just saying 'twins' makes me feel tired already." My twins were born in February this year, 10 weeks early and, honestly, the word "tired" does not even begin to describe our preterm twin parenthood journey over the past five months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been a tiring, exhausting, sleepless five months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My eye bags are now almost permanent and bigger than my eyes most of the time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But at the same time, in between the crying, the screaming, the burping, the poo and pee, the nappy leaks and the vomits, the past five months have bought us so much happiness, smiles, love and made me appreciate things a lot more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On 23 February, my wife called me telling me her water bag broke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will never forget that call but, honestly, the rest of that day was a complete blur.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I did rush home, picked her up and rushed to the hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That evening, they performed an emergency caesarean and Katie and Poppy were born, 10 weeks premature.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I wanted to be in the operating theatre with my wife but the doctor did not allow it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He replied that "There will be a lot of doctors and nurses in there as they have to deliver twins and your twins might come out lifeless and will have to be resuscitated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It might be too traumatic for you to see this." Waiting for them to come out of the operating theatre was one of the most excruciating waits of my life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was a very difficult and painful 10 weeks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was an absolute emotional roller coaster ride and it was physically draining.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were at the hospital every day, watching them progress and then deteriorate, progress and deteriorate, progress and deteriorate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was painful watching them stop breathing, their heart rates plummet in front of my very eyes and, at times, their lips turning blue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nothing can properly describe the feeling of watching your babies go through that repeatedly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is an experience I wish no parent has to go through.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And my babies were not the smallest, the most premature there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There were babies at the NICU who weighed only 800 grammes and I cannot even begin to imagine the amount of stress, pain and trauma their parents were going through.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This first chapter of the journey was also perhaps the most difficult as I did not take my paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I could not, as I wanted to save the precious two weeks for when Katie and Poppy came home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Every time my phone rang, my heart skipped a beat as it might be from the hospital with bad news.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The dilemma I faced would be the same dilemma all fathers of preterm babies face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like Jeremy Chee, who also had preterm twins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In his own words, "Most of the time is spent shuttling between home and hospital and being a Uber milk delivery dad.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: By the time they were discharged, I had spent most, if not all, of my paternity leave." This was the same situation for Yeo See Yeong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He said, "Taking care of a preterm baby is already tough, let alone preterm multiples".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Pearlyn Ong, a mother of preterm twins said, "As I had a C-section, I really needed the help of my husband at home and to bring the twins to the polyclinic since I was recovering from my wound.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, he has no more leave left by the time both babies came home." It was the same for Gina Tan, whose husband ran out of paternity leave while her premature twins were still in hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And, worse still, for Agatha Kee who had one twin in hospital and one twin discharged.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She had to take care of them in two different places.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In her words, "It's mentally and physically straining".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The 16 weeks of maternity leave are supposed to be to bond with your baby.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This bonding is crucial, as stated by Mr Chan Chun Sing, then-Acting Minister for Social and Family Development, in his closing speech for the Child Development Co-Savings Bill in 2013.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He said, "Maternity leave caters to the time required for the mother to physically recuperate from childbirth and nurse the infant before returning to work".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, by introducing two weeks of mandatory paternity leave from 2017, MSF had recognised the importance for fathers to have the "opportunity to actively bond with their children from the time they are born" as it is a "critical infant period".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first few months with your baby are important few months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But these 16 weeks of bonding are clearly reduced for parents of preterm babies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Having spent so much time in NICU, I can tell you that proper bonding is almost impossible there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Babies are often in incubators, making physical contact with them very difficult.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Holding the babies is also difficult as most have several tubes attached to them and there is, of course, the risk of passing an infection to the babies, which could be deadly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My twins spent 10 weeks in hospital and it is little, compared to others.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Stephenie Tan's premature daughter spent 103 days in KK Women and Children's Hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She had no choice but to return to work three weeks after her baby came home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot imagine having to go back to work when your baby is discharged after spending 16 weeks in hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I doubt anyone can function properly at work in any case.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Worse still is going back to work when your baby is still in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was the case for Meiyan Carol who had premature twins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "The twins are my first babies so after giving birth and seeing them with all the tubes and equipment really scared me and I couldn't stop worrying.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Every day, I will visit them in NICU for those few short hours, I couldn't help but break down several times." One of her twins was discharged after three months, the other after seven months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She went back to work after taking her maternity leave and after her elder twin was discharged, she had no choice but to take two months of unpaid leave to take care of her.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And this is the case now for Ng Hui Wen, whose premature daughter is currently warded in KK Women and Children's Hospital for over four months already.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She took only two months of maternity leave, as she wanted to save the remaining two months to spend with her baby when she is discharged.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In her words, "The daily visits to hospital has taken a toll on my mental and physical health".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And the time the baby spends in hospital is an important time for both fathers and mothers to be together rather than apart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The emotional stress is tremendous and both parents need to be there for their babies and for each other.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Magdaline Lee, a mother of a preterm baby said, "I had to admit I had postnatal depression when I saw my two-kilogramme baby in NICU with tubes over him.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The need to have a supporting husband during this period is crucial to the family.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Having just two weeks of paternity leave wasn't enough for me, I needed to have someone to be there emotionally and mentally after going through an unexpected early delivery." Perhaps the most heart-wrenching story shared with me was that by May Leo who had premature twins but one twin caught an infection in her womb and could not be saved.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The other twin stayed in hospital for about four months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "My husband and I, especially me, had to manage losing a baby and running to and from the hospital during my confinement to be with my baby boy during his critical days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It was very tiring and sad at the same time".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And it is important to be there for also the babies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Doing kangaroo care or skin-to-skin contact with the baby does help the baby grow better as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Kangaroo care is commonly prescribed for preterm and low birth weight babies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been found to have wide-ranging benefits for both infant and parents, including reducing infant mortality, increasing growth, raising likelihood and duration of breastfeeding, encouraging mother-infant bonding and increasing parental satisfaction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lee-Ling Chow, who has premature twins, told me she was glad that her company allowed her to take no-pay leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Similarly, Anitha Narayanan was allowed to take all her annual leave and one month of no-pay leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I exhausted my four months of maternity leave and had to apply for another three months of unpaid leave to take care of my baby." Rachel Lee's twins spent two months in the hospital before they came home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "Luckily, my boss has allowed me to take another three to four months of unpaid leave to look after the girls until they were bigger and more stable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what about other moms who didn't have understanding superiors like mine?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They could have lost their jobs." And some do pay the price.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yongle had premature twins and took three months of hospitalisation leave and four months of maternity leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She said, "I was lucky enough to keep my job but with pay freeze and a 50% cut to my year-end bonuses." I sincerely hope the Government can make sure parents of premature babies are not penalised.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This leave can also be transferred to the father.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In Denmark, maternity leave is prolonged by the period the infant spends in the hospital for up to three months, if the infant is hospitalised during the first 46 weeks of childbirth.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This change in policy while significant for parents of preterm babies, really would not be a significant change for employers who might be worried about the manpower shortage or the Government in terms of the additional financial resources for the paid leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Babies born before 37 weeks are considered preterm but, unfortunately, I could not find data on the number of births before 37 weeks in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it is usually babies who are born before 28 weeks who would require a longer stay at the hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is also clearly verifiable with doctors when a baby needs to be in hospital, especially NICU.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, there need not be concerns about abusive leave applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The next chapter of the journey could perhaps be summed up by one word, too, which is the word I started this speech within the opening paragraph "tired".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These two days were among the happiest days of my life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were overjoyed to bring Katie and Poppy home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were overjoyed to finally see them without any tubes stuck into them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were overjoyed to finally introduce Katie and Poppy to Ella, our eldest daughter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For 10 weeks, she could only see them through a glass window and she really wanted to carry them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was also the time we realised that our two babies were, in fact, owls.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They were full-fledged party owls and completely nocturnal and they partied through the night.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I rarely use the word sleep now as I cannot really remember what sleep is and what it feels like to sleep properly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the first few months, the twins needed to be fed every two to three hours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It took about 30 minutes to feed each baby.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My wife took about 30 minutes to express the breast milk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After feeding, it takes about 10 minutes to wash and sterilise all the bottles and pumping equipment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not forgetting that their nappies have to be changed before each feed and that takes about five minutes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And it takes another five minutes to burp each baby.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It might sound a bit gross but I now absolutely love the sound of burps.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hearing a burp means I can finally rest or sleep.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the problem is the end of the cycle is pretty close to the start of the next cycle and, if you can see where I am heading, sleep is a valuable commodity when you have twins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problem is not when the twins cry at the same time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, I feel it is better that they do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is worse when you finally calm one down and the other one starts crying.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I have responded to Minister Ong Ye Kung's call to continually upgrade my skills and I have evolved to meet the changing needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have gone from feeding one twin at a time to feeding both at the same time, holding one milk bottle in each hand to last month, I have mastered the art of feeding both twins at the same time with just one hand.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just last week, I managed to feed one twin and burp the other twin at the same time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Now, I have to try and see if I can burp both of them at the same time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I know my wife would be horrified if I tried it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents of multiple births have to deal with greater challenges than parents of single births.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Multiple birth parents are more likely to have less sleep because their babies can have different sleep-wake rhythms and express their needs at different times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Multiple birth parents have little chance to regain their strength and are more likely to remain tired for an extended period of time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents of multiple births also have greater need for an extra pair of helping hands, such as from their partner, to help care for multiple babies at once.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, 93% of British multiple birth mothers wished that their partners had extended paternity leave to help care for their babies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Beyond these, parents of preterm babies and multiple births also have much more medical appointments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the past few months, Poppy alone has had repeated medical appointments with the ophthalmologist, cardiologist, speech and language therapist, physiotherapist and neonatologist.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A lot of time has been spent back at the hospital.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, as you can see from my eye bags, parents of twins need help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If you see my wife's eye bags, you know that we really, really need help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many countries already offer extended parental leave in cases of multiple births, some offering it since 1975.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These countries include Finland, Norway, Sweden, Germany, Luxembourg, Portugal, Spain, Austria, Belgium, France, Czech Republic, Latvia, Poland, Russia, Israel, Turkey and, closer to home, China, South Korea, Japan, Vietnam and Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In France, for example, maternity leave is extended by 18 weeks for twins, by 30 weeks for higher order multiple birth.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In Myanmar, maternity leave is extended by four weeks for twin deliveries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Like preterm babies, this change in policy will not have a big overall impact.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Parents also cannot choose whether they have twins or triplets and, so, they cannot manipulate the system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot end this speech without thanking the amazing doctors, nurses, therapists, cleaners and all the staff members at the delivery suites, NICUs and High Dependency Units at SGH and all the other hospitals. "Thank you" for saving the lives of Katie and Poppy and countless other babies they have cared for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At times, it was surreal sitting at the NICU, doing kangaroo care with my baby, singing to her while watching the mayhem in NICU.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Watching the staff handle a never-ending arrival of preterm babies and a never-ending chorus of alarm bells as babies stop breathing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The staff members handle each situation so professionally, so meticulously and with so much tender loving care.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From the bottom of my heart and on behalf of all the other parents, thank you.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also wanted to highlight the efforts of the Facebook group "SG Parents of Twins and Triplets" which has been the only form of communal support for parents with multiples.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And, Madam, through this journey, I also realised that I have married Wonder Woman.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She has also mastered the art of pumping breast milk while feeding both twins at the same time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unfortunately, I definitely would not benefit from these changes, as my factory is closed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With three daughters, I am heavily outnumbered at home already and this factory is definitely permanently closed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This one I really love. "Twins will make love stronger, Days shorter, nights longer, Bank account smaller, Home happier, Clothes shabbier, The past forgotten and The future worth living." Thank you, Madam.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He spoke from the heart and won us over with not just the strengths of his arguments but also the intensity of his conviction.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And I think I can reasonably speak for everyone in the House that we are all very glad to hear that Katie and Poppy are back home from the hospital and that the whole family is doing well, notwithstanding your lack of sleep.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have a lot of sympathy for all the challenges that parents like Mr Ng go through, having had twins myself and also nieces who were born prematurely.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not everyone appreciates the unique challenges Mr Ng highlighted.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After all, multiple births constitute just 3% of all children born in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, the number of preterm births at 35 weeks or below is relatively low, about 4.5% of births.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These numbers have remained stable over the past decade.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although the numbers are not large, the impact on each family is significant; I think we heard from Mr Ng.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For this reason, I agree fully with Mr Ng that there is scope to consider how we can better support parents with preterm babies or who have to manage multiple births.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government is strongly committed to supporting Singaporeans in their marriage and parenthood journey.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, we have progressively enhanced support measures over the years, which include legislating new leave provisions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, maternity leave has been increased twice: in 2004, it went up from eight to 12 weeks; in 2008, from 12 to 16 weeks.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To support fathers in playing a more active role, paternity leave and shared parental leave were introduced in 2013 and were enhanced just this year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Fathers now have two weeks of paternity leave and can share up to four weeks of their wife's maternity or adoption leave, as shared parental leave.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our parental leave provisions are also fully paid.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In comparison, while some other countries provide longer periods of leave, much of the leave provisions are paid partially or not at all.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even so, as Mr Ng has highlighted, parents may have greater care-giving needs when their infants are born prematurely, or if there are two or more babies at one go.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Public sector officers can get an additional four weeks of unpaid leave when they have children below the age of one.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will give parents the option to take more leave if they need to.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Depending on the outcome of the pilot when it ends in 2020, we will assess the possibility of a nationwide rollout in future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the meantime, given the significant enhancements made to parental leave provisions recently, we will need to give employers some time to adjust before considering further legislative changes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While more leave could be useful for parents who have multiple or premature births, we have to be mindful that we do not inadvertently affect their employability if they are absent from work for an extended period of time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers have provided feedback that increasing leave provisions could have an impact on manpower and administrative costs, especially in a time of business uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For practical reasons, we will always need to balance between providing support for employees with caregiving needs and employers' concerns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond parental leave, there are also other measures in the Marriage and Parenthood Package which support parents, including those with multiple or premature births.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Mr Ng noted, the Baby Bonus cash gift and Child Development Account co-savings are given on a per-child basis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All children receive the Medisave Grant for newborns of $4,000, and are covered under MediShield Life from birth, including for any congenital or neonatal conditions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These measures help to defray the costs of their children's healthcare and medical needs and provide parents with greater peace of mind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Parents have given the consistent feedback that while the parenthood support measures are helpful, they also need employers to provide a family-friendly work environment.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am glad to hear from the examples that Mr Ng cited, that many employers are, indeed, understanding and helpful.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We encourage more employers and co-workers to show understanding towards parents who may have extenuating circumstances and require more time to care for their children after birth.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, private companies can join the public sector in taking the lead to provide additional unpaid leave to parents of infants.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: According to a survey by MOM, in fact, more than half, 54% of establishments in 2016 provided unpaid leave of more than one month for employees to attend to family or personal matters.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another useful form of support is flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers can tap on various resources to implement flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, the tripartite partners are jointly developing a Tripartite Standard on Flexible Work Arrangements, which will help job-seekers and employees identify progressive employers with strong support for flexible work arrangements.
